subject: [RFC PATCH 3/5] mm/page_alloc: convert any movable pageblock on a non-movable allocation

reviews.author: Dev Jain
reviews.summary: Reviewer Dev Jain noted that the patch series as-is would regress performance by having many unmovable pageblocks with movable allocations, which could hurt memory-transparent huge pages (mTHP) allocations.
reviews.raw_body:
I think your patch series applied as-is would regress stuff:
we may have lots of UNMOVABLE pageblocks with lots of
movable allocations, unable to be rescued, hurting mTHP
allocations.

reviews.author: Rik Riel (author)
reviews.summary: Author is seeking feedback on how to proceed with the patch series, asking reviewers whether they want to review each patch individually before an update or post the entire series at once.
reviews.raw_body:
How should we move forward with this?

Do do guys want to review this series first,
and then I post an update with the other
stuff, before any gets merged?

Or do you want me to post a larger series
all at once?

Before I move on, do the combined policy
changes from patches 3, 4, and 5 make sense
to you (with or without evacuation) ?

Patch 1 from this series can be merged all
by itself as a separate thing.

-- 
All Rights Reversed.

2026-10-15.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of try_to_claim_block() to convert any movable pageblock on a non-movable allocation, regardless of how many pages are free or compatible. This ensures that the block's type matches the allocation it serves and prevents non-movable content from being stored in movable-typed blocks. The patch also introduces stricter rules for converting non-movable pageblocks to movable, requiring all pages to be free or movable before claiming a block. Additionally, blocks straddling zone edges are never claimed due to their potential for inconsistent behavior.
